verses.text: In the church at Antioch there were prophets and teachers: Barnabas; Simeon, who was called Niger; Lucius from Cyrene; Manaen, who had grown up with Herod the ruler; and Saul.
While they were worshiping the Lord and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, “Set apart Barnabas and Saul for me. I’ve called them to do this work.”
After fasting and praying, they laid their hands on Barnabas and Saul and sent them off.
Sent out by the Holy Spirit, they went down to Seleucia and sailed from there to Cyprus.
In Salamis they shared God’s message in the Jewish synagogues. John was there helping them.
They traveled across the island to Paphos, where they met a Jewish sorcerer and false prophet named Bar-Jesus.
He was with the governor, Sergius Paulus, an intelligent man. The governor called for Barnabas and Saul because he wanted to hear God’s message.
But Elymas the sorcerer—that’s what his name means—opposed them, trying to turn the governor away from faith.
Then Saul, also called Paul, filled with the Holy Spirit, stared straight at Elymas
and said, “You’re full of lies and every kind of trickery, child of the devil and enemy of everything right! Will you ever stop twisting the Lord’s straight paths?
Now look: the Lord’s hand is against you. You’ll be blind for a while and won’t see the sun.” At once, mist and darkness covered him. He stumbled around, looking for someone to guide him.
When the governor saw what happened, he believed. The Lord’s teaching amazed him.
Paul and his companions sailed from Paphos and reached Perga in Pamphylia. John left them there and went back to Jerusalem.
They continued from Perga to Antioch in Pisidia. On the Sabbath, they went into the synagogue and sat down.
After the Law and the Prophets were read aloud, the synagogue leaders sent them a message: “Brothers, if you have something to encourage the people, go ahead and speak.”
Paul stood up, motioned with his hand, and said, “People of Israel—and everyone here who honors God—listen up.
The God of this people chose our ancestors. While they lived as outsiders in Egypt, God made them a great people and brought them out with mighty power.
He put up with them in the wilderness for about forty years.
Then he overthrew seven nations in Canaan and gave his people their land as an inheritance. That took about 450 years.
After that, he gave them judges until the time of Samuel the prophet.
Then they asked for a king, and God gave them Saul son of Kish, from Benjamin’s tribe. He ruled for forty years.
After removing Saul, God raised up David as their king. God testified about him: ‘I’ve found David, Jesse’s son, a man after my heart. He will do everything I want.’
From David’s family line, God brought Israel a Savior, Jesus, just as he promised.
Before Jesus came, John had already announced a baptism calling Israel to turn back to God.
As John finished his work, he said, ‘Who do you think I am? I’m not the one. But someone is coming after me, and I’m not even worthy to untie his sandals.’
“Brothers, descendants of Abraham, and all of you who honor God: this message of salvation has been sent to us.
The people of Jerusalem and their leaders didn’t recognize Jesus. They didn’t understand the words of the prophets read every Sabbath, and by condemning him they fulfilled those very words.
Though they found no reason to put him to death, they asked Pilate to have him killed.
After carrying out everything written about him, they took him down from the cross and placed him in a tomb.
But God raised him from the dead!
For many days he appeared to the people who had traveled with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are now his witnesses to the people.
“We’re bringing you good news: God made a promise to our ancestors,
and has fulfilled it for us, their descendants, by raising Jesus from the dead. As the second Psalm says, ‘You are my Son; today I have become your Father.’
“God raised Jesus from the dead, never to decay again. He said, ‘I will give you the holy and sure blessings I promised David.’
That’s why another Psalm says, ‘You won’t let your Holy One decay.’
David served God’s purpose in his own generation, then died and joined his ancestors. His body decayed.
But the one God raised did not decay.
So, brothers and sisters, hear this: through Jesus, forgiveness of sins is announced to you.
Everyone who believes in him is made right with God—something Moses’ Law could never do for you.
So watch out, or what the prophets warned about may happen to you:
‘Look, you mockers! Be amazed, then disappear! I’m doing something in your days that you wouldn’t believe even if someone explained it to you.’”
As Paul and Barnabas were leaving the synagogue, the Gentiles begged them to share this message again the next Sabbath.
After the meeting, many Jews and devout converts followed Paul and Barnabas. The two urged them to keep living in God’s grace.
The next Sabbath, almost the whole city gathered to hear God’s message.
When some Jewish leaders saw the crowds, jealousy took over. They argued against Paul’s words and insulted him.
Paul and Barnabas spoke boldly: “God’s message had to be shared with you first. But since you push it away and judge yourselves unworthy of eternal life, we’re turning to the Gentiles.
The Lord commanded us to do this: ‘I’ve appointed you as a light for the Gentiles, to bring salvation to the ends of the earth.’”
When the Gentiles heard this, they were glad and praised the Lord’s message. Everyone God had appointed for eternal life believed.
Then the Lord’s message spread throughout the whole region.
But some Jewish leaders stirred up devout, influential women and the city’s leading men. They sparked persecution against Paul and Barnabas and drove them out of the region.
So Paul and Barnabas shook the dust off their feet against them and went to Iconium.
The disciples were filled with joy and the Holy Spirit. ✨
